Life from age 4 to 16

I like making dinner work from the first step to the point where people can eat. That does not mean I want to run a restaurant, and I would rather see an actual kitchen schedule before deciding how far to take it.

  • family: Lives with her father and two younger siblings; aunt provides occasional childcare.
  • finances: Tight but stable income; home cooking is part of the normal routine.
  • geography: San Marcos, Texas.
  • cultureLanguages: English and Spanish across relatives; family shares recipes informally.
  • school: Public high school with general electives and a supervised food event.
  • accessOpportunities: Home kitchen and school-event guidance; no commercial kitchen work.
  • Age 4–5

    In 2014, Sky liked pretend picnics and choosing which small plate each toy should use. She also enjoyed building sand roads and did not show much interest when adults tried to teach her the names of ingredients.

  • Age 6–7

    At six, she began helping wash produce and arrange simple snacks. During 2017, she learned that having everything ready before starting made a shared kitchen less confusing, especially when younger siblings wanted to help at the same time.

  • Age 8–9

    In 2018, Sky tried a music club and an outdoor group without wanting to continue either. At home she enjoyed adjusting a family recipe, but did not yet think of cooking as a special activity needing a label.

  • Age 10–11

    During 2020, she helped plan the order of dinner tasks while her father handled work. Several attempts ran late, and she learned to start the longest step first rather than beginning with whichever ingredient she liked preparing.

  • Age 12–13

    At twelve, Sky was making several family meals each week with appropriate adult support. In 2023, she began comparing recipe versions and paying closer attention to safe storage and the timing of food prepared for others.

  • Age 14–15

    Across 2024 and 2025, a supervised school food event let her try a larger sequence of tasks. She liked preparing food, while bargaining, supervising people, and imagining restaurant ownership did not become appealing simply because cooking remained enjoyable.

  • Age 16

    At sixteen in 2026, Sky is exploring Texas culinary demonstrations and training information. Many unrelated activities still feel uncertain or uninteresting, and she wants to learn about kitchen hours, conditions, and costs without being pushed toward management or business ownership.

Life now

  • enjoys: Recipe tests · Cooking sequence · Preparing food for others
  • avoids: Bargaining · Staff supervision · Restaurant ownership
  • activities: Several family meals weekly · Supervised school food event
  • demonstratedSkills: Plans familiar cooking steps · Compares recipe versions · Uses household safety routines
  • unfamiliarActivities: Commercial kitchens · Large-service food safety · Restaurant hours
  • motivations: Useful meals · Improving a concrete process
  • ambitions: Observe a training kitchen before choosing study · She imagines a steady home life with shared meals and enough personal time outside work.
  • struggles: Uncertain about many unrelated activities · Larger-scale work may differ from home
  • supports: Father · Aunt · School event supervisor
  • practicalConstraints: Sibling routines · Training fees · No commercial exposure

Still uncertain: How will commercial pace affect enjoyment? · Does cooking remain satisfying when hours and menus are externally set?

Pathways: Food, hospitality & personal care

Work-led options: None featured.

Field explored: services. Sky enjoys testing recipes and planning the sequence until people can eat, with household safety routines. She explores food preparation without treating that as a wish to supervise staff or own a restaurant.
